note: Practice problem 18.23 with a straight neck: flange, R19 dome with its R3 dome/neck blend revolved to y 45, a Ø22 pipe on y 24 out to z 50, R3 on the pipe junction. That fillet runs over the dome sphere, the torus and the neck, and OCCT approximates it as a B-spline face with a C0 knot (and C0 edge curves). BRepOffset refuses C0 before it tries any join, so every shell of a body filleted like this was refused with C0Geometry (2026-09-16). Split at the C0 knots first, the 3 mm shell open at the flange bottom, neck top and pipe end builds valid. Checked offline: every sampled inner-wall point is exactly 3 mm from the outer surface, except near the three openings, where the open face itself is nearer; none is farther.
